Winnipeg visits St. Louis tonight with the model leaning slightly toward the home side, projecting 3.06 expected goals (the quality of chances, not just the count) for STL against 2.79 for WPG. At five on five, STL has taken 51% of the expected goals in its games and WPG 46%, so there isn't much between them, though the Jets give up more good chances (3.38 per 60 minutes against 3.03). On special teams, WPG's power play (0.61 expected goals per game) is stronger than STL's (0.49), and STL takes 3.88 penalties a game against 3.12 for the Jets. The Jets are also missing Josh Morrissey (wrist), who is on injured reserve.

In net, the projected goalies are Stuart Skinner for WPG and Joel Hofer for STL, both at a .906 save percentage this season. Skinner has saved 2.82 goals above expected, which measures how many goals he has stopped beyond what the shots he faced would normally allow, against 1.28 for Hofer. Last season Hofer was well ahead at 11.05 over 46 games, while Skinner was at 5.96 over 50. Both teams are 2-2-1 in their last five, but STL took 54% of the expected goals in those games while WPG took 45%.

Among the players to watch, Kyle Connor is the most likely Jet to score at 40%, though he's flagged as due to cool. Mason McTavish brings a six-game point streak (4 goals, 4 assists) and a 30% chance to score for St. Louis. Dylan Holloway has a four-game point streak and a 60% chance of a point.
